frequency_question: How often do threatened major trade tariffs against close allies actually take effect on the initial deadline rather than being delayed, watered down, or averted via agreement?
membership_rule: Includes: explicit presidential announcements of major tariffs with a specific implementation date against developed allies (Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan, South Korea). Excludes: broad anti-dumping/countervailing duties by independent agencies (ITC/DOC) and routine safeguard investigations.

cases.name: Trump steel and aluminum tariffs on Canada, Mexico, and EU
Trump threatened 5% escalating tariffs on Mexico over migration
Trump threatened 100% tariffs on French wine over digital services tax
Trump threatened 25% tariffs on all Mexican imports re USMCA ratification
Trump reinstated 10% aluminum tariffs on Canada

coverage_note: 5 named major executive tariff threats against close allies with firm deadlines; believed roughly 7-8 in total across modern U.S. administrations.
known_gaps: Excludes minor bilateral disputes or threats made solely via unverified social media without formal administrative backing.
validity_reason: Relies on presidential trade negotiation style which may shift significantly with future administrations.
